newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent weakens as heating oil turns negative.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent weakens as heating oil turns negative.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures fell sharply in the afternoon session as heating oil failed to provide impetus for an upward move, brokers said.
Nov Brent fell to a low of $21.85 a barrel, down 14 cents, shortly after the NYMEX open, where heating oil dumped 62 cents to $66.80 a gallon.
"It's coming off because the front end of the cash market is on the sloppy side and heating oil has shown negative numbers this afternoon and shown willingness to come off," a floor trader said.
IPE gas oil held at $217.00 a tonne, up $3.00 a tonne.
"While heating oil was providing strength on Friday and overnight and crude was a reluctant player, now that heat is coming off crude is coming down to more comfortable levels," the trader said.
He added Monday's levels were likely to set the tone for the rest of the week now that Gulf tensions had eased and the Iraq factor was no longer contributing to price volatility.
Concerns over the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin translated into a firmer IPE open but brokers said this was not necessarily bullish as it was unlikely to affect oil exports.
